description:
## Goal

Make each closed compiler/runtime operation one sealed, typed World declaration with one declarative semantic contract. An intrinsic identity is carried from runtime bootstrap through lowering, guard planning, interpreter, JIT, and AOT without a source-name lookup, a handwritten duplicate signature, or an operation-specific semantic reconstruction.

The prior implementation is invalid: it introduced user-visible `intrinsic "..." fn` syntax, resolved a quoted selector only during lowering, repeated declarations in `lib/kernel.fz`, and reconstructed bool, pid, ref, send, and resource semantics in `LoweredIntrinsic::validate`. Those are multiple semantic authorities and contradict this ticket.

## Correct model

The closed runtime descriptor inventory is the sole declaration authority. Each entry owns:

- its opaque `Intrinsic` identity and Kernel binding;
- a compiler-neutral semantic signature shape: exact parameter/result types, type variables, bounds, and correlations;
- runtime representation admission domains;
- effect, guard-admissibility, and fault behavior.

Runtime bootstrap uses that inventory to publish typed intrinsic callable facts into the exact Kernel runtime-module namespace/interface on demand. The World fact carries `Intrinsic`, not a selector string. The ordinary source/lowering path then consumes that fact as it consumes any callable identity. Kernel retains only human-facing wrappers; it does not hand-declare intrinsic leaves.

There is no `intrinsic` parser syntax, quoted-surface case, `NativeDeclaration::Intrinsic(String)`, string-to-identity resolver, validator-as-second-contract, name-based interpreter interception, or handwritten Kernel intrinsic declaration. Generic `extern` remains for actual foreign symbols and continues to own ABI/marshalling. Runtime and compiler may mechanically lower an `Intrinsic` differently, but they consume the same descriptor and cannot restate semantic signature, correlations, effects, or faults.

`spawn_opt` has no observable semantic contract: interpreter and scheduler paths discard its heap hint. Delete the public `Kernel.spawn/2` heap-hint surface and its `SpawnOpt` identity, runtime hook, FFI, fixtures, and documentation; `spawn/1` remains the sole spawn primitive. Do not retain an admitted-but-inert argument or an implementation-only compatibility path.

## Strategy and deletion

First trace the existing runtime bootstrap, `FunctionDefined`/namespace publication, function contract, lowering, and exact fact ownership. Reuse those authorities; do not add a registry, source scanner, name keyed map, parallel signature resolver, synthetic display-name lookup, or global bootstrap pass. The descriptor must be projected into the existing demand-driven source/function facts so an unchanged request retains allocations and a cold runtime intrinsic remains cold until requested.

Write focused red tests before construction for: exact identity present before lowering; descriptor-derived bool/pid/ref/type-variable/resource contracts; no source spelling authority after normal callable resolution; no parser acceptance for `intrinsic`; no generic extern/dlsym/marshalling route for an intrinsic; exact cross-door execution/fault/effect behavior; deleted `spawn/2`; unchanged and unrelated requests starting no new work. Then delete the obsolete parser, quoted-source, surface, declaration, resolver, validation, interception, ABI, hook, fixture, documentation, and test scaffolding as the fact producer replaces them.

## Acceptance

- One descriptor-derived declaration proves the semantic contract for every intrinsic; no operation match outside the descriptor reconstructs result types, opaque brands, variable bounds, or correlations.
- World owns the typed intrinsic declaration before `LowerFunction`; lowerer, semantic analysis, guard dispatch, interpreter, JIT, and AOT consume its identity directly.
- The runtime prelude publishes only demanded intrinsic facts and replaces/withdraws exact owned contributions without rescanning global state.
- All intrinsic execution doors agree on input admission, result, effect, and fault behavior. Tests inspect typed identity/facts and deterministic work telemetry rather than rendered names.
- `intrinsic` is absent from accepted user syntax and compiler special cases; `lib/kernel.fz` contains wrappers only, not intrinsic leaves.
- `spawn_opt` and all inert heap-hint paths are removed, with no compatibility shim.
- Existing true extern declarations keep their ABI and marshalling authority.
- Full focused, library, fixture, CLI, check, strict Clippy, format, deterministic reuse/artifact gates pass; docs describe only the final model.
- No probe, migration adapter, duplicate declaration, compatibility path, or stale documentation remains.

## Causality

This ticket is blocked by fz-tfn.69, which first restores truthful PR boundaries. It blocks fz-tfn.62: GuardDispatch must consume the final World-owned typed intrinsic identity, not the rejected string/declaration model.

## Review

Fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review must independently count semantic authorities, verify all descriptor consumers derive rather than reconstruct semantics, audit bootstrap/fact causality and coldness, and inspect the PR boundary before one replacement commit and close.
title: Give runtime intrinsics one typed declaration and semantic authority
